sections.2025 (Auburn): Started all 18 matches and totaled 1,134 minutes … Totaled five goals and three assists for 13 points … Placed over half of her 40 shots on frame (.550 SOG) … Scored a pair of goals against Southern Miss for her fifth career brace … Assisted twice against Kennesaw State … Headed in the game-winner with less than 10 minutes remaining against Texas A&M … Scored at No. 12 Mississippi State to help the Tigers secure their first of three results against top-20 opponents on the season … Played a career-high 80 minutes in Auburn’s first match with LSU … Earned SEC Academic Honor Roll distinction for the second-straight year … Named to the SEC Preseason Watch List and United Soccer Coaches Forwards to Watch List.
sections.2024 (Auburn): Earned United Soccer Coaches fourth-team all-region honors … Second Team All-SEC … Named to the SEC Academic Honor Roll … Led the team with 11 goals and 25 points and also added three assists … Became the first Auburn player in eight years to record double-digit points … Started all 21 matches of the season, playing 1,112 minutes … Led Auburn with 46 shots, placed 26 on frame (.565 SOG) … Became the first Auburn player in seven years to record three braces in one season, scoring a pair of goals against South Alabama, Samford and Tennessee … Earned three points with a game-winning goal and an assist on the road at LSU … SEC Offensive Player of the Week Sept. 9 after scoring two against Samford and the game-winner against No. 17 Ohio State.
sections.2023 (Auburn): Played in 19 matches and made five starts while logging 589 minutes … Scored two goals … Made her collegiate debut starting at left winger against Samford and recorded three shots in 54 minutes of action … Scored her first two collegiate goals against American on Sept. 3, netting the game-winner in the 38th minute and scoring again in the 74th minute … Became the first Tiger freshman to score a game-winner since the 2020-21 season and the first freshman to notch a brace since 2019..
sections.High School/Club: Graduate of Monacan High School … Two-time first-team all-state and All-Metro… Two-time First Team All-State selection … Member of A/B Honor Roll, NHS, Beta Club, Morgan’s Message Club & Tribe Club … Played club soccer for Richmond United, which won the 2021 Richmond Regional … Team captain and leading goal-scorer for Richmond United in 2022.
sections.Personal: Full name is Olivia Sinclair Woodson … Born in Richmond, Va. … Parents are Tonya and Milton Woodson … Has an older brother, Evan … Decided to attend UCLA because “I felt Ilike I could have impact on the team and develop with the coaching and staff here” … Describes her greatest athletic thrill as scoring against Mississippi State, where her former coach had previously coached … Athlete she admires are Trinity Rodman, Simone Biles and LeBron James … Interests include shopping, trying new food, traveling and doing cosmetic things … Project management major with a career objective to be a nurse practitioner. ] ]

sections.2025: Earned third-team All-Big Ten honors … Named to the Academic All-Big Ten team and earned a Big Ten Distinguished Scholar Award … Played in all 21 games and made eight starts … Tied for third on the team in points scored with seven, recording two goals with three assists … Scored the game-tying goal at Michigan State in the regular season and assisted on the game-winning goal at Michigan three days later … Scored the game-winner against Iowa … Assisted on the game-winning goal against Pepperdine in the NCAA first round … Totaled 36 shots, including a team-leading 22 on goal … Played in a season-high 66 minutes at Wisconsin.
sections.2024: Played in the last nine games of the season and started in the last five … Scored her first collegiate goal just over a minute into the NCAA First Round game against Cal Baptist … Recorded her first point in the Big Ten Championship win over Rutgers, assisting on the game-winning goal … Made her season debut on Oct. 13 at Illinois.
sections.U.S. National Team: Played with the U-19s at the L’Albir U-19 Women’s International Tournament in February 2025 … Selected to the U.S. U-19/U-18 training camp in March 2025 … Invited to attend the U.S. U-17 National Team training camp in June 2023.
sections.High School/Club: Led Chamblee HS to the 5A State Championships during her sophomore and junior years … Named the 5A Co-Player of the Year … Played club soccer for Concorde Fire … Two-time ECNL Southeast Conference Player of the Year and All-American.
sections.Personal: Full name is Kara Ashley Croone … Born in Atlanta, Ga. … Parents are Tricia and Eric Croone … Has an older brother, Eric … Decided to attend UCLA because of the academics, athletics and the coaching staff … Describes her greatest athletic thrill as leading her team to their first state championship, scoring a hat trick in the semifinals … Athletes she admires include Serena Williams, LeBron James, Lionel Messi, Simone Biles, Kobe Bryant and Kylian Mbappé … Interests include baking, photography and playing the piano. ] ]

sections.2025: Played in all 21 games and made six starts … Ranked third on the team with three goals and tied for third in scoring with seven points … Named the Big Ten Freshman of the Week Sept. 2 after scoring the game-winner and assisting on a second goal in the Bruins’ 2-0 win over Long Beach State … Also scored a goal in the Bruins’ win over Nebraska and scored in the final minute to seal a 3-1 win over Pepperdine in the NCAA first round.
sections.High School/Club: Played three years of soccer and four years of track & field … Offensive MVP of 6-6A and second-team all-region honors in 2025 … Earned first-team all-district honors and was named the midfielder of the year in 2024 … Newcomer of the Year in 2022 … Played club soccer with Solar Soccer Club and won the national championship in 2023.
sections.Personal: Born in Plano, Texas … Mother is Donnita Gordon … Decided to attend UCLA because of the campus, environment and welcoming nature of the team … Greatest athletic thrill is doing celebrations after goals with her teammates … Admires boxer Terence Crawford and basketball player Anthony Edwards … Hobbies are fishing, listening to music, baking and watching old soccer games, crime documentaries, baking shows and Animal Kingdom … Hopes to become a neurologist. ] ]

sections.2025: Named to the Academic All-Big Ten team … Did not play due to an offseason injury.
sections.2024: Big Ten Freshman of the Year and All-Freshman selection … Earned third-team All-Big Ten honors … Top Drawer Soccer Freshman Best XI first-team selection … Started and played in 20 games … Helped UCLA’s defense record a nation-leading 16 shutouts and 0.41 goals against average … Her first collegiate goal was the game-winner in the Big Ten quarterfinals against Penn State … Named to the Top Drawer Soccer Preseason Freshman Team.
sections.U.S. National Team: Member of the U.S. U-20 Women’s National Team pool … Played on the 2022 U.S. U-17 World Cup team and the 2022 U.S. U-17 Concacaf Championship team … Invited to the England International camp in 2023 and the Spain International camp in 2022 … 2023 Pan American Games participant.
sections.High School/Club: Two-time letter winner at Rock Canyon HS … Named an All-American and Offensive MVP of the Continental League during her junior year … First-team CHSAA All-State selection in 2023 … Ranked the No. 12 recruit in the nation … Played club soccer for Real Colorado … Earned ECNL U-15 All-America honors … Two-time first-team ECNL All-Mountain Conference.
sections.Personal: Full name is Nicola Marley Fraser … Born in Littleton, Colo. … Parents are Ashley Albrecht and Robin Fraser … Has an older sister, Dani … Father Robin played with the U.S. Men’s National Team and was a two-time Major League Soccer Defender of the Year with the Los Angeles Galaxy and Columbus Crew … Describes her greatest athletic thrill as playing Chile’s senior team in Chile at the Pan American Games … Decided to attend UCLA because of the academics and athletics … Athletes she admires are Chloe Kelly, Alphonso Davies, Chloe Kim, and Carlos Alcaraz … Hobbies include reading baking, mountain biking, skiing, traveling and hanging out with her sister. ] ]

sections.High School/Club: Earned one letter for soccer at Beacon High School in New York, N.Y. before graduating early to enroll at UCLA in Winter 2026 … Was captain for her high school team … Played for Downtown United Soccer Club and was club captain … Trained with Gotham FC 2 in the offseason.
sections.Personal: Full name is Fiona McGeough … Resides in Manhattan … Parents are Lauren and Paul McGeough … Has an older brother, Finnegan, an older sister, Leila, and a younger sister, Imogen … Decided to attend UCLA because it has been her dream school since she visited the campus as a little girl: “I fell in love with the campus and school pride. When I stood at the top of Pauley Pavilion and saw the Bruin statue, I knew this was the place I wanted to be one day. I have also always strived for high academic and athletic achievement, and UCLA is the perfect balance of both.” … Describes her greatest athletic thrill as the pregame huddle with her team … Lists famous athletes she admires as Jalen Brunson, Ryan Gravenberch, Thiago Alcantara, Sergio Busquets, and Lionel Messi … Hobbies and interests include baking, boating, basketball, soccer, STEM, rescuing dogs, and swimming … Has fostered two dogs with her mom growing up. ] ]

sections.Canadian National Team: Helped lead Canada to the quarterfinals of the 2025 U-17 Women’s World Cup … Competed with the U-17s at the Four Nations Cup, U-17 Concacaf Qualifiers, and the U-17 MIMA Cup in 2025.
sections.High School/Club: Played soccer, hockey, basketball, cross country, track, badminton, field hockey and flag football at Nepean High School … Ranked number one in Canada’s class of 2026 three times by First Touch Football … Played club soccer for Futuro Soccer Academy and NDC Ontario … Played with French club Le Havre at the 2023 U-19 Essonne Cup … Also a standout hockey player, she attended the Ontario Provincial U-16 Development Camp and played in the Ontario Summer Games.
sections.Personal: Full name is Molly Eileen Hale … Born in her hometown of Ottawa … Parents are Mike Hale and Julia Lamb … Has one younger brother, Declan … Her great-great uncle Jimmy McGrory played soccer for Team Scotland and Celtic FC and is Celtic FC’s all-time leading scorer with 522 career goals … Chose to attend UCLA because she loves the style of play, the team culture, the school history and the strong academics … Greatest athletic thrill was representing Canada at the U-17 Women’s World Cup … Athletes she admires are Neymar, Marinette Pichon, Jessie Fleming, Robinho, Allan Iverson and Désiré Doué … Hobbies include playing all sports, baking and spending time with her dog … Career objective is to be a professional soccer player. ] ]

sections.High School/Club: Four-year letterwinner for soccer at Cathedral Catholic HS … Was also a three-year letterwinner in track & field, running the 400m, 300 hurdles, 100m and 200m … Lettered one year in flag football as a safety and wide receiver … Earned the CIF-SDS Flag Football Sportsmanship Award in 2025 … Helped her track & field team win the FIC-SDS championship in 2022 and 2024 … Played club soccer for Rebels FC … Aided her club team in winning the ECNL Conference Cup - Southwest Division in 2025.
sections.Personal: Full name is Anna Grace Wilson … Born and raised in San Diego, Calif. … Parents are Elizabeth and Brian Wilson … Her father Brian played water polo for the U.S. Naval Academy … Mother Elizabeth was on the Notre Dame cheer team … Her grandfather played football for Kansas, and her grandmother played basketball for Xavier University … Has two younger brothers, Josh and Sam … Decided to attend UCLA “because of the combination of top-tier soccer and top-tier academics”; she also loves the team culture, coaching staff and players … Describes her greatest athletic thrill as winning the Western League with her high school team in 2025 … Admires Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone for her humility and composure and Michael Jordan for his competitiveness … Hobbies include surfing, skating, snowboarding and spending time outside … Major is Business Economics. ] ]

sections.Brazilian National Team: Attended six camps for the Brazil U-17 National Team and one camp for the Brazil U-20 national team … Competed in the 2024 Under-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup … Earned a silver medal with her team in the 2025 U-17 South American Tournament.
sections.High School/Club: Earned two letters for soccer at West Torrance High School … Played club soccer for Beach FC.
sections.Personal: Full name is Isabela Lins Araújo … Born and raised in Torrance, Calif. … Has a sister, Júlia … Chose to attend UCLA “because of the elite environment, strong history of the program and love of sports culture that the school has. I wanted to be a part of a program that is competitive and nurtures the growth and development of its athletes while doing so.” … Describes her greatest athletic thrill as representing Brazil at the U-17 Women’s World Cup, saying “To be able to represent my country at the highest level in that age group was like living a dream. It was an honor to defend that jersey and play beside and against the best in the world.” … Lists famous athletes she admires as Cafú, Trent Alexander Arnold and Lucy Bronze … Hobbies include going to the beach, watching soccer and crochet … Career objective is to be a professional soccer player. ] ]
